analysis: The code snippet calls `buffer.deleteCharAt(buffer.length() - 1);` only if the last character is ':', which implies that `buffer.length()` is at least 1. The earlier check `if (buffer.length() > 0)` ensures that the buffer has content. After appending, the length is positive, so the index `buffer.length() - 1` is valid (within [0, length-1]). Therefore, `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` is avoided.
remark: The only declared exception, StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, is avoided because the index used (length-1) is guaranteed to be valid due to the prior length check and the conditional check on the last character before deletion.
